doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Reflections on the life of a musician
title: Surviving drug dealers and debts
summary: Ware says dealers followed bands, and he owed rent and a debt on pay.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: -- the guys could survive at it and people, geniuses, could survive that. I hear people talking about Bird and drugs or something. But the fact that he could play so much music under those conditions --

-- is phenemonal. It has happened. He was damned by not only the fellas he played with, but some of the people that he played for, because they were the people that was feeding off him. Oh, shoot, we had -- I had guys, you know, on the road -- they'd follow us from engagement to engagement. The man was going to be there with the stuff, you know, and I worked one club out there in Chicago, the guy would sit right there. I think I was making ten dollars a night. See, that's $60 for six nights, and $60 I owe him.
